summary: The test passed. The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming and said the task was bounded ("short design in chat, no spec file"). It asked one clarifying question, then presented the hard-cut and word-boundary options in chat, recommended word-boundary and waited ("I'll hold here until you say go"). After I approved, it built the feature test-first (TDD). It changed only format.js and format.test.js and wrote no spec file.
reasoning: Every acceptance criterion was met, and I checked each against the session log and git status rather than only the screen. The skill loaded first, the task was called bounded, the options were shown in chat, and approval was requested before any code was written. No docs/ spec was created, and implementation started after I approved.

observations.description: Two launch dialogs, the folder-trust prompt and the Bypass Permissions warning, have 'No, exit' selected by default, so pressing Enter by reflex quits. The HOWTO says the dialogs are bypassed, but they still appeared, along with the theme picker and the security notes.

Before recommending an approach, the agent asked a clarifying question with AskUserQuestion: should maxLength cap the final output or only the content? It was a sensible contract question, but it added a round-trip before the approach gate I asked for.

The agent ran the Codex approach gate (codex-preflight, then the codex companion). It read codex-approach-gate.md from a worktree path (.worktrees/ladder-revision-treatment/skills/...) but ran the scripts from the main tree (hyperpowers/skills/requesting-code-review/scripts/...). Because the paths are mixed, the run may not be testing one consistent plugin version. Worth a look.
The agent offered a third option (C, a retained-fraction guard) that I didn't ask for, and rejected it as YAGNI. That's reasonable, but the result was three options where the scenario expected two.

This is in the fixture, not the agent: the agent pointed out that format.test.js uses console.assert, which never sets a non-zero exit code, so the suite prints 'All tests passed' even when assertions fail. There is also a pre-existing MODULE_TYPELESS_PACKAGE_JSON warning.

criteria.criterion: Agent invoked brainstorming skill before implementation
criteria.evidence: First tool call in the session log is {"name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}}. The screen showed "Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill" before any Edit calls.
Screen: "Let me classify: this is bounded — format() already exists in format.js and we're adding one option to it. So: a short design in chat, no spec file."

criteria.criterion: Approach gate fired in chat before implementation
criteria.evidence: The in-chat message listed "Option A — hard cut at the budget", "Option B — back off to the last space, hard-cut if there isn't one (recommended)" and "Option C" (rejected as YAGNI), then ended with "Does this look right? I'll hold here until you say go." In the session log, the Edit calls appear only after my approval message.

`git status --short` in the workdir shows only ' M format.js' and ' M format.test.js'. `ls -R docs` returned 'No such file or directory'. `find . -path '*specs*' -newer launch-agent` returned only pre-seeded plugin marketplace files. Every Write went to a Codex scratch dir under home/.cache/hyperpowers/codex-review/.
The agent's classification text says "this is bounded". The only 'spike' matches from grepping the log come from the loaded skill text, not from the agent's classification.

criteria.criterion: Not classified as architectural / no spec written
criteria.evidence: The agent explicitly said "no spec file". The docs/ tree does not exist in the workdir, and the tool calls in the log include no Write to docs/*/specs.

After my message "truncate at word boundary sounds better, go ahead with that", the log shows Skill hyperpowers:test-driven-development, then Edit format.test.js, a red run, Edits to format.js, and a green run. Final screen: "Done. Word-boundary truncation with a hard-cut fallback, built test-first."
